claims.text: The resistance of high-entropy-alloy multilayer coatings to time-dependent plastic deformation is jointly governed by oxide dispersion and individual layer thickness.
Individual layer thickness influences interface density.
The proposed initial Ti0.2CoCrFeNi multilayer coating contains a nanoscale oxide dispersion.
Nanoscale oxide particles act as dislocation-pinning agents.
Changing individual layer thickness changes the density of interfaces in the coating.
Dislocation pinning and increased interface density reduce dislocation mobility.
Reduced dislocation mobility increases resistance to time-dependent plastic deformation.
Resistance to time-dependent plastic deformation increases as oxide-dispersion content increases over the proposed range.
Resistance to time-dependent plastic deformation increases as individual layer thickness decreases over the proposed range.
At sufficiently high oxide content, oxide-induced embrittlement limits the expected improvement.
Interlayer delamination limits the expected improvement in resistance.
The proposed oxide-dispersion-content boundary is 1–10 vol%.
The proposed individual-layer-thickness boundary is 10–100 nm.

contradictions.description: The initial state is defined as already containing a nanoscale oxide dispersion, whereas the intervention is described as introducing a nanoscale oxide dispersion. It is unclear whether the intervention adds oxide to an oxide-free coating or varies an existing dispersion.
